properties.decision:
ACCEPTED on Anthony's word, 2026-09-01, against the recommendation that the zero-cost option be tried before any mechanism is added.

THE PROBLEM, restated so this stands alone: reflow2 models the USER's word thoroughly and the AGENT's almost not at all. An agent holding a correct substantive answer to an open question has `answer_question` — whose own description is "record what the USER said" — and `acknowledge_gap`, which refuses an unknown approver. Using either would put the agent's reasoning in the user's mouth, so it stays quiet, and the silence is indistinguishable from having nothing to say.

⭐ THE PRACTICE, AND IT USES ONLY WHAT ALREADY EXISTS: the agent records its reasoning as a `proposed` Decision, linked to the question it answers, with the human named as approver. That is attributed, visible, reported by `loop_status` until answered, and impossible to mistake for the owner's word. It costs one node and no new vocabulary.

🛑 AND NOTHING IS BUILT UNTIL THAT IS SHOWN INSUFFICIENT. `dec:idea-should-the-agents-own-word-get-a-first-class-record` — generalising `proposed` + approver to gap answers, acknowledgements and possibly requirement status — STAYS OPEN and is deliberately not taken here. The reason is the one that decision named against itself: every record type that gains a proposed state gains a lifecycle, and lifecycles are where designs rot. Four states across six node types is twenty-four combinations nobody has thought about, bought to solve a problem the existing mechanism may already solve.

📌 WHAT WOULD REOPEN IT — named now, so the condition is on the record rather than in somebody's memory, and because this design has just been reminded what a parked decision is worth when it says what would unpark it (`chg:the-prescribed-layer-pairs-stop-refusing`): a case where the proposed-Decision practice is tried and is genuinely the wrong shape — an answer that has no natural decision to hang off, or one where the linked-Decision route loses information the gap needed to keep.
properties.name: DECIDED — an agent with a substantive answer records it as an open Decision linked to the question, and nothing new gets built until that is shown insufficient
properties.rationale:
RECORDED AS ITS OWN DECISION rather than as a status change on the idea it defers, because they are different claims: "adopt this practice" is settled, and "generalise the mechanism" is not. Collapsing them would either assert a generalisation nobody approved, or lose the practice that WAS approved.

⚠️ THE HONEST WEAKNESS, and it is the reason a reopening condition is written above: this is the cheap option chosen partly BECAUSE it is cheap. Nobody has yet tried the practice on a real gap and found it sufficient — the evidence for it is an argument, not a measurement, which is a weaker footing than this project usually accepts. What makes that acceptable here is the asymmetry of cost: the practice can be abandoned in a session, and a lifecycle across six node types cannot.

📌 IT ALSO DOES NOT TOUCH THE ANTI-FORGERY RULE, which stays exactly as it is. `acknowledge_gap` still requires the owner's name, `answer_question` still records what the user said, and requirement status still moves only on their word. Nothing here relaxes any of that; it gives the agent a place to stand that was always available and never named.
